DIAGNOSIS READY: Hip Dislocation (Posterior) with associated Femoral Head Fracture.

Based on your history of a rear-end collision, immediate severe right groin pain, abnormal leg positioning (typically flexed, adducted, and internally rotated in posterior dislocations), and lack of significant past medical history, the clinical picture strongly suggests a traumatic hip dislocation, potentially with an associated femoral head fracture. The initial X-ray requested should confirm the dislocation and rule out acetabular or femoral fractures. Immediate reduction and orthopedic consultation are critical to prevent avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
